headline: HSC results deferred to Oct 31
summary: Over 1.27 million candidates await their results, which were originally scheduled for October 29.
details: The results of this year’s HSC and equivalent examinations will be published on October 31, two days later than previously announced.
The Bangladesh Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee announced the revised date in a notice issued yesterday.
The results will be announced at 11:00 am at the International Mother Language Institute in Dhaka and made available simultaneously at educational institutions and online.
Students can check their results through their respective education boards’ websites or from their institutions. Results will also be available via SMS.
Applications for re-scrutiny will be accepted online from November 1 to 7, with details available on the education boards’ websites.
A total of 1,270,583 candidates registered for this year’s HSC and equivalent examinations under 11 education boards.

headline: 400 deaths: Dengue death toll reaches 400 as cases turn severe
summary: Health experts warn of delayed diagnosis and hospitalisation as a larger proportion of patients arrive at hospitals in critical condition.
details: At least 11 dengue patients died yesterday, bringing this year's total death toll to 400. According to the Directorate General of Health Services, 128,237 patients have been hospitalised nationwide so far this year.

While overall admissions are declining, doctors report that a higher proportion of patients are arriving in critical condition. Many are suffering from dengue shock, characterized by undetectable blood pressure and falling oxygen saturation.

Experts warn that delays in diagnosis, transportation, and admission are causing irreversible damage to vital organs. Timely use of intravenous fluids and blood products is crucial for recovery in these severe cases.

This year has seen an increase in severe complications, including liver, kidney, respiratory, and heart failure. The circulation of dengue virus serotype 3 (DENV-3) and repeat infections are cited as potential contributing factors.

Elderly people, those with obesity, and patients with underlying health conditions are identified as the most vulnerable groups. Specialists urge people to seek immediate medical advice if they develop fever or body aches.

To prevent dehydration, patients are advised to drink sufficient fluids and ORS. Paracetamol can be used for fever under guidance, but other painkillers should be avoided unless prescribed by a doctor.

Public health experts suggest piloting free dengue testing at primary healthcare facilities. A comprehensive approach involving community prevention and timely referrals is needed to reduce the death toll.
caption:
The dengue death toll has hit 400. Doctors warn that patients are arriving at hospitals in far more critical condition than in previous years.

At least 11 dengue patients died yesterday, bringing this year's total death toll to 400. According to the Directorate General of Health Services, 128,237 patients have been hospitalised nationwide so far this year.

While overall admissions are declining, doctors report that a higher proportion of patients are arriving in critical condition. Many are suffering from dengue shock, characterized by undetectable blood pressure and falling oxygen saturation.

Experts warn that delays in diagnosis, transportation, and admission are causing irreversible damage to vital organs. Timely use of intravenous fluids and blood products is crucial for recovery in these severe cases.

This year has seen an increase in severe complications, including liver, kidney, respiratory, and heart failure. The circulation of dengue virus serotype 3 (DENV-3) and repeat infections are cited as potential contributing factors.

Elderly people, those with obesity, and patients with underlying health conditions are identified as the most vulnerable groups. Specialists urge people to seek immediate medical advice if they develop fever or body aches.

To prevent dehydration, patients are advised to drink sufficient fluids and ORS. Paracetamol can be used for fever under guidance, but other painkillers should be avoided unless prescribed by a doctor.

Public health experts suggest piloting free dengue testing at primary healthcare facilities. A comprehensive approach involving community prevention and timely referrals is needed to reduce the death toll.
